mainTopic: The opinion of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר on storing, and the new משנה on the amounts of animal feed one must carry out on שבת to be liable (with the dispute about carrying feed in a measure meant for one animal but intended for another)
overview: This amud opens with רבי אלעזר noting that the previous משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, once one person stores an item, anyone who carries it out is liable. A new משנה then lists how much of each animal feed (straw, עצה, grain stalks, grass, onion and garlic leaves) one must carry out on שבת to be liable. It also rules that the different feeds do not combine toward one measure. The גמרא defines עצה as legume straw. It then brings רב דימי's report of a dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a cow's mouthful of straw carried for a camel. In רבין's version, everyone agrees that case is liable. The real argument is about a cow's mouthful of עצה for a cow, and it depends on whether 'eating under pressure' counts as eating. The גמרא shows that the משנה's measure for עמיר and a ברייתא's measure are really the same amount. רבי יוסי בר חנינא then says that different feeds do combine toward the more lenient measure. The גמרא challenges him from the case of cloth, sack, leather and mat, which combine only because they share טומאת מושב. רבא begins his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The previous משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the previous משנה, which makes only the person who stored the item liable, does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: This ruling is not in line with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר is commenting on the end of the previous משנה. He says it does not match the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous משנה ruled that if someone stored an item that people do not normally store, only he is liable for carrying it out. Everyone else is liable only for a normal-size amount. רבי אלעזר points out that a different תנא disagrees, and the next step quotes that תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: This (referring to the ruling just learned)
A תנא whose view is about to be quoted

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: This is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
phrases.notes: "This" refers to the previous משנה's ruling that only the person who stored the item is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the previous משנה (from the prior daf)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The previous משנה's limitation of liability to the person who stored the item does not match רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא: one person's storing makes everyone liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Once one person stores an unusual item, anyone who carries it out is liable because of the first person's intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated a rule. Take anything that is not normally fit to store, and that people do not usually store. If it became fit for this one person and he stored it, and then someone else came and carried it out, the second person is liable because of the first person's thinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view. This is the proof for what רבי אלעזר just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view, one person's storing gives the item importance for everyone. So even a different person who carries it out is liable. In our משנה, only the one who stored it is liable, and that is why the two sources disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
To store or put away for later use

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, one person's intent to store something gives it importance for everyone. Our משנה limits that importance to the person who stored it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a rule:
Anything that is not fit to be stored,
and people do not store things like it,
but it became fit for this person and he stored it,
and another person came and carried it out —
this one is liable because of the thought of that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רבי אלעזר's claim
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees with the previous משנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's general rule

steps.title: משנה: the measures for carrying out animal feed
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the minimum amount of each kind of feed that makes a person liable for carrying it out on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who carries out straw is liable for a cow's mouthful. For עצה, the measure is a camel's mouthful. For grain stalks, it is a lamb's mouthful. For grass, it is a goat's mouthful. For garlic leaves and onion leaves, if they are moist, the measure is a dried fig. If they are dry, it is a goat's mouthful.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists how much of each type of animal food a person must carry out on שבת to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each food is measured by the animal that normally eats it, and by how much that animal takes in one mouthful. Moist onion and garlic leaves are eaten by people, so they get the human-food measure, a כגרוגרת. Dry leaves are only animal food, so they get a goat's mouthful.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of the משנה)
One who carries out (from a private to a public domain)
A type of coarse animal feed (defined later in the גמרא)
The size of a dried fig, the standard measure for human food

steps.confusionAlert: Each measure depends on the animal that eats that food. A cow's mouthful is the measure for straw only. It is not a general measure for all animal feed.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא תֶּבֶן — כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה.
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who carries out straw — a cow's mouthful.
Etza — a camel's mouthful.
Grain stalks — a lamb's mouthful.
Grass — a goat's mouthful.
Garlic leaves and onion leaves:
if moist — a dried-fig size,
if dry — a goat's mouthful.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא תֶּבֶן כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on new measures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each kind of feed has its own measure for liability, based on the animal that eats it.

steps.title: The different feeds do not combine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that these foods cannot be added together toward one measure, because their measures are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these do not join with one another, because their measures are not equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a rule. You cannot put together half a measure of one food and half a measure of another to make one full measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each food has its own standard measure. Since the measures are different, there is no shared standard to add them up against. So partial amounts of different foods stay separate.

keyTerms.meaning: Combine or join together toward a measure

steps.whatToRemember: Each feed has its own measure, and different feeds do not combine because their measures are not the same.

phrases.english: And they do not combine with one another
because they are not equal in their measures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule to the list of measures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different feeds do not combine toward liability, because their measures differ.

steps.title: What is עצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word עצה in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is עצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the meaning of an unclear word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עצה is not a common word, and its measure (a camel's mouthful) is unusual. To understand the rule, we first need to know what this food is.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (marks the start of the discussion)

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is etza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word עצה

steps.title: עצה is legume straw
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that עצה is the straw of legume plants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is straw from types of legumes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. עצה is the stalks of bean-type plants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legume straw is very coarse, and mainly a camel can eat it. That explains why the משנה measures it by a camel's mouthful.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Straw of types of legumes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: תֶּבֶן שֶׁל מִינֵי קִטְנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עצה is the straw of legumes, which is coarse camel feed.

steps.title: רב דימי reports a dispute: a cow's mouthful of straw for a camel
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about someone who carries a cow's mouthful of straw intending it for a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: Take one who carries out a cow's mouthful of straw for a camel. רבי יוחנן said he is liable. רבי שמעון בן לקיש said he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רב דימי brings a dispute from ארץ ישראל about carrying a full measure for one animal while intending it for another animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cow's mouthful is a full measure for straw, but it is too small to feed a camel. רבי יוחנן looks at the amount itself, which is a full measure, so he says liable. ריש לקיש looks at the person's purpose, which is too small for a camel, so he says exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
An אמורא who often brought teachings from ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא תֶּבֶן כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה לְגָמָל,
phrases.english: One who carries out straw, a cow's mouthful, for a camel —
Rabbi Yochanan said: liable.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's measures to a mixed case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: רבי יוחנן says liable, and ריש לקיש says exempt, for a cow's mouthful of straw intended for a camel.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן ruled 'liable' in the evening, but took it back in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the evening, רבי יוחנן said this. In the morning, he took it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי continues his report. רבי יוחנן later reversed himself and agreed with ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the reversal, both אמוראים hold 'exempt' in this version. The next two steps argue about whether this change of mind was correct.

phrases.english: In the evening, Rabbi Yochanan said this;
in the morning, he retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאוּרְתָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי, לְצַפְרָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב דימי's report
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן retracted and now holds 'exempt'.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the retraction was correct
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף approves of רבי יוחנן's retraction, because a cow's mouthful is not enough for a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: He did well to retract, since it is not enough for a camel!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his opinion on the retraction and supports it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's reasoning is that the person's own purpose decides. The person meant the straw for a camel, and for a camel this amount is meaningless. So there is no liability.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
He did well that he retracted,
since it is not fit for a camel!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שַׁפִּיר עֲבַד דַּהֲדַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the retraction and supports it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person's intended use decides, and a cow's mouthful is meaningless for a camel.

steps.title: אביי: the original view makes more sense
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the opposite. The original 'liable' is more logical, because the amount is significant for a cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary, the original view makes more sense, since it is fit for a cow.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף. He argues that רבי יוחנן's first ruling was the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, what counts is the amount itself. A cow's mouthful of straw is a real, useful amount, because a cow could eat it. So the person carried out something significant, even if his own plan was to feed a camel.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical, it makes sense

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
On the contrary, the original view is more reasonable,
since it is fit for a cow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reasoning
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's approval of רבי יוחנן's retraction
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The amount is objectively significant because it can feed a cow. The person's plan to feed a camel should not cancel that significance.

steps.title: רבין's version: everyone agrees the straw case is liable
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a different version of the dispute. In the straw-for-a-camel case, everyone agrees the person is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when Ravin came, he said: One who carries out a cow's mouthful of straw for a camel — everyone agrees he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets aside רב דימי's report and brings רבין's version instead. In this version, the straw case is not argued at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here everyone holds like אביי's logic. A full cow's mouthful of straw is significant on its own, so the person is liable no matter which animal he meant it for. That means the real dispute must be about a different case, which the next step gives.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who also brought teachings from ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: רבין is not adding a new opinion inside רב דימי's report. He is giving a completely different account of what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argued about.

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא תֶּבֶן כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה לְגָמָל,
phrases.english: One who carries out straw, a cow's mouthful, for a camel —
everyone agrees that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב דימי's version of the dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow's mouthful of straw carried out for a camel makes one liable, according to everyone.

steps.title: The real dispute: a cow's mouthful of עצה for a cow
steps.stepSummary: According to רבין, the argument is about someone who carries a cow's mouthful of עצה, intending it for a cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is when one carries out a cow's mouthful of עצה for a cow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין names the case that is really argued about. It is a small amount of camel feed that the person intends for a cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the משנה's standard, עצה needs a camel's mouthful, so a cow's mouthful is too little. But this person plans to feed a cow, and for a cow that amount is a full meal. The question is whether his purpose can make this small amount count. The next step tells us who holds which side, and why.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבין's version, the full measure of straw always makes one liable. The disputed question is whether a person's purpose can make a smaller-than-normal measure (עצה intended for a cow) count. The next step gives each side.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the question to a sharper case: can personal intent raise the importance of an amount that is below the normal measure? The same idea appears in the earlier storing discussion with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: Where they disagree

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹצִיא עָצָה כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה לְפָרָה.
phrases.english: is in one who carries out etza, a cow's mouthful, for a cow.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, בְּמוֹצִיא עָצָה כִּמְלֹא פִי פָרָה לְפָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבין's version by naming the case that is truly in dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree about a cow's mouthful of עצה intended for a cow.

steps.title: The reversed version of the dispute and the reason behind each side
steps.stepSummary: In רבין's version the positions are reversed compared to רב דימי's report: רבי יוחנן says exempt and ריש לקיש says liable. Their argument is whether 'eating under pressure' counts as eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the opposite was reported: רבי יוחנן said exempt, and ריש לקיש said liable. רבי יוחנן said exempt, because eating under pressure is not called eating. ריש לקיש said liable, because eating under pressure is called eating.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין continues. In the עצה-for-a-cow case, the positions are the reverse of רב דימי's report: רבי יוחנן says 'exempt' and ריש לקיש says 'liable.' The גמרא then explains the reason behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is food that an animal eats only when it has no choice, like hard עצה straw. If that kind of eating does not count, carrying it is not carrying 'animal food,' so the person is exempt. If it does count, he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite was reported (the names of the two opinions are swapped)
Eating under pressure – food eaten only when there is no other choice

steps.whatToRemember: The core question is whether food that is eaten only when there is no choice still counts as 'food' for the measure of הוצאה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the versions. In this reversed version, רבי יוחנן is the one who says 'exempt,' and ריש לקיש says 'liable.'

phrases.english: And the opposite was stated:
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: exempt,
Reish Lakish said: liable.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said exempt —

phrases.aramaic: אֲכִילָה עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק לֹא שְׁמָהּ אֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: because eating under pressure is not considered eating.
Reish Lakish said liable —

phrases.aramaic: אֲכִילָה עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק שְׁמָהּ אֲכִילָה.
phrases.english: because eating under pressure is considered eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבין's report by assigning the positions in the עצה case (reversed relative to רב דימי's version) and stating the principle behind each.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether אכילה על ידי הדחק counts as eating decides liability. רבי יוחנן says it does not (exempt), and ריש לקיש says it does (liable).

steps.title: Lamb's mouthful versus a dried fig
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the measure for עמיר as a lamb's mouthful, but a ברייתא says a dried fig.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: עמיר – a lamb's mouthful. But a ברייתא taught: the size of a dried fig!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and points out that a ברייתא seems to give a different measure for the same item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources seem to disagree on how much עמיר makes a person liable. One says 'a lamb's mouthful' and the other says 'a dried fig.' The גמרא needs to show these do not really conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as fills a lamb's mouth
A dried fig – a standard measure for liability on שבת
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: An ear of grain: equivalent to a lamb's mouthful.
But wasn't it taught: equivalent to a dried fig!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's measure for עמיר (a lamb's mouthful)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא gives a different measure (a dried fig) for the same item, so the sources seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: Both measures are the same amount
steps.stepSummary: A lamb's mouthful and a dried fig are the same size, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: This and that are one measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two measures are really the same amount, just described in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody is arguing here. A lamb's mouthful happens to equal the size of a dried fig, so the משנה and the ברייתא agree.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one – both

phrases.english: This and that
are one measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: two descriptions of one amount
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא give different amounts for עמיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A lamb's mouthful equals a dried fig, so both sources agree.

steps.title: The leaf measures, and the rule that the different feeds do not combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה again: wet leaves need a dried fig's size and dry leaves need a goat's mouthful. None of the listed feeds combine with one another, because their measures differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Garlic leaves and onion leaves: wet ones – the size of a dried fig; dry ones – a goat's mouthful. They do not combine with each other, because their measures are not equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, which sets two measures for leaves and says they cannot be added together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet leaves are human food (measure: a dried fig), while dry leaves are animal food (measure: a goat's mouthful). The closing clause covers all the feeds in the משנה. Since each has a different measure, partial amounts of different feeds (for example, straw and grass) do not add up to make a person liable. The next step, by רבי יוסי בר חנינא, limits this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as fills a young goat's mouth
Combine (are added together to reach a measure)

phrases.english: Garlic leaves and onion leaves,
moist: equivalent to a dried fig,
and dry: equivalent to a goat's mouthful,
and they do not combine with one another
because they are not equal in their measures.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items with different שיעורים do not combine to make a person liable.

steps.title: They combine toward the lenient measure, not the strict one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא limits the משנה: mixed items do not reach the stricter (smaller) measure, but they do reach the more lenient (larger) measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: they do not combine toward the stricter one among them, but they do combine toward the more lenient one among them.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא explains that the משנה's 'they do not combine' is only partly true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you mix the two kinds, you cannot reach the smaller (stricter) measure, because the lenient item does not count toward it. But if you reach the larger (lenient) measure, the stricter item certainly counts toward it, since it is even more significant.

keyTerms.meaning: The stricter of them (the one with the smaller measure)
The more lenient of them (the one with the larger measure)

steps.whyThisMatters: This limitation is exactly what the גמרא is about to challenge.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
They do not combine toward the more stringent among them.
But they do combine toward the more lenient among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's rule that items with different measures do not combine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items with different measures combine toward the larger (lenient) measure but not toward the smaller (strict) one.

steps.title: Do things with different measures ever combine? The case of cloth, sack, leather and mat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether unequal measures can combine at all. It brings the טומאה case of different materials and a ברייתא saying they do combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do things whose measures are not equal combine at all? But we learned: cloth – three by three; sack – four by four; leather – five by five; mat – six by six. And a ברייתא taught on it: cloth with sack, sack with leather, leather with mat – they combine with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts challenging רבי יוסי בר חנינא by bringing a משנה and a ברייתא about טומאה. This step sets up the source, and the real point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each material has its own minimum size to become impure, yet the ברייתא says pieces of different materials combine. The גמרא will now ask why they combine, and the reason will show that combining is an exception, not the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And a ברייתא was taught about it

steps.confusionAlert: This case does not prove רבי יוסי בר חנינא right. The גמרא brings it in order to argue against him, and the next step shows how.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל דְּלָא שָׁווּ בְּשִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ מִי מִצְטָרְפִין?
phrases.english: And do any items that are not equal in their measures combine?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
The garment — three by three handbreadths,
and the sack — four by four,
and the hide — five by five,
a mat — six by six.
And it was taught about it in a baraita:
The garment and the sack, the sack and the hide,
the hide and the mat —
combine with one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל דְּלָא שָׁווּ בְּשִׁיעוּרַיְיהוּ מִי מִצְטָרְפִין? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 17 that unequal measures combine toward the lenient measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule that items with unequal measures combine toward the lenient measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It suggests that unequal measures normally do not combine at all. It brings a source where they do combine in order to show, in the next step, that this happens only for a special reason.

steps.title: They combine only because they share the use of מושב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the materials combine because each can become impure as a seat (מושב). So things without such a shared use would not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון said: What is the reason? Because they are fit to become impure as a seat. So the reason is that they are fit to become impure as a seat; but if something is not fit to become impure as a seat – no, it does not combine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It reads a precise inference from רבי שמעון's reason: combining happens only when there is a special shared use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four materials can be used to patch a saddle, so they share the category of טומאת מושב, and that is why they combine. Without that shared use they would not combine, even toward the larger measure. This seems to contradict רבי יוסי בר חנינא, who says unequal items always combine toward the lenient measure.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to become impure as a seat (through a זב sitting on it)
The reason is X; but without X – no (a precise inference)

steps.whatToRemember: From רבי שמעון's reason we learn that items with different measures combine only when something special unites them. That challenges רבי יוסי בר חנינא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This inference is what gives the challenge against רבי יוסי בר חנינא its force, so the גמרא will have to answer it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason —
because they are fit to become impure as a seat.
The reason is that they are fit to become impure as a seat;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין רָאוּי לִיטַמֵּא מוֹשָׁב — לָא!
phrases.english: but what is not fit to become impure as a seat — no, it does not combine!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דִּרְאוּיִין לִיטַמֵּא מוֹשָׁב, אֲבָל אֵין רָאוּי לִיטַמֵּא מוֹשָׁב — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 18 by drawing an inference from רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that items with unequal measures generally do not combine at all (against רבי יוסי בר חנינא)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's reason in the ברייתא on כלים: they combine only because they are fit for טומאת מושב
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule (step 17) that items with unequal measures combine toward the lenient measure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון explains that the materials combine only because they all share fitness for טומאת מושב. This implies that without such a shared use, items with different measures do not combine at all, even toward the larger measure.

steps.title: רבא begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement by רבא. It will respond to the difficulty from Steps 18-19 about whether things with different measures can combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: רבא is about to speak. This line only names the speaker, and his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 18-19, the גמרא learned from רבי שמעון that different materials combine only when they share a common use. That made it hard to accept רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule in Step 17 that the משנה's different feeds combine toward the more lenient measure. רבא's coming statement on the next amud responds to this difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, a leading אמורא of Babylonia

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a ruling in this line. It is only the opening of רבא's statement, and the content comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: Attribution formula. It opens רבא's statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a response to the difficulty raised by רבי שמעון's reasoning in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces רבא's upcoming statement.
